newsitem.title: USA: Travelers holders end staggered board.
newsitem.headline: Travelers holders end staggered board.

text.p: Shareholders of Travelers Group Inc at the annual meeting Wednesday overwhelmingly approved a proposal to end the staggered election of directors, in which one-third of the board members were elected each year.

According to a preliminary count, 99 percent of the votes cast, or 77 percent of the outstanding shares, voted to amend the incrorporation certificate and "declassify" the board so that holders will now vote on all 21 board slots each year.

In his remarks to the shareholders, chairman and chief executive Sanford Weill noted that the Standard & Poor's Corp, Moody's Investors Service Inc and Fitch Investors Service in the last two months have all raised ratings on Travelers Group debt.
He further noted that S&P observed that approximately two-thirds of the financial group's earnings are derived from predictable and recurring sources.
Noting that mergers are taking place "all across the financial services industry" Weill said Travelers wants to be ready "when the right opportunities present themselves."

In some general references to possible acquisition strategy, Weill said "we don't believe in our company being a (financial) supermarket." He also said there is "no better time" to improve a company's position "as it relates to what is happening in the world market."

He said he favors "fairness" and functional regulation in the U.S. financial services market so that all players can compete in all areas. He noted that Bankers Trust New York Corp is buying Alex. Brown Inc but current law prevents Alex. Brown from buying more than 4.9 pct of Bankers Trust. "That does not sound like the American way," he said.

Asked by a shareholder to comment on the effect or rising interest rates, Weill said the company "is not very sensitive" to a change of 100 to 150 basis points in interest rates. But he said there could be a negative effect on markets and if the company's stock fell people might want to buy more shares.

Weill said the Internal Revenue Service is currently reviewing the company's plan to put what are known as "WealthBuilder" options for employees into employee 401(k) plans. Approval is also needed from the U.S. Department of Labor. A company spokeswoman said that if approved, it would be the first use of such options in a 401(k) plan.
